item.title: Set up, build, and test
item.description:
Use a repository checkout to build Larecs and check a change against its locked toolchain. The supported Pixi platforms are Linux x86-64 and macOS Apple Silicon. Application installation has a separate guide.

Install and smoke-test

From the repository root, install the locked environments and run the checked movement program:

pixi install --locked
pixi run mojo --version
pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/movement.mojo

The program prints All particles reached their expected positions. after asserting the results. The root manifest declares Mojo >=1.0.0,<1.1.0, MAX >=26.5.0,<27, and mojo-tracy >=1.1.0,<2; pixi.lock pins the actual resolution. Retain the reported compiler build with verification evidence. The separate scripts environment pins documentation tools.

Build a package

Precompile the source package, then build an example against that package:

pixi run mojo precompile src/larecs -o /tmp/larecs.mojoc
pixi run mojo build -I /tmp examples/particles/movement.mojo -o /tmp/larecs-movement
/tmp/larecs-movement

This checks package consumption without -I src. The final program must produce the same result as the source smoke run. CI also performs a package smoke check; generated packages are disposable build outputs.

Run focused checks, then the suite

For a storage-lifecycle change, run the focused test before the full suite:

pixi run tests test/host_storage_lifecycle_test.mojo
pixi run tests test
pixi run test-resource-compile-failures

The test wrapper precompiles Larecs and uses assertions, debug information, tracing linkage, and AddressSanitizer unless a file opts out. A full directory run also executes compile-contract checks and bounded core/spatial performance checks. Focused files trigger their associated contracts but omit performance checks. The resource compile-failure fixture task is a separate CI step. Use test and hardware coverage to select the right checks and interpret device skips. Optimized performance measurements need separate untraced, unsanitized binaries.

Resolve platform failures

Symptom Action
Metal compiler crashes compiling a GPU iterator with -g Add # SKIP_DEBUG to every GPU-launching test. Keep the actual GPU path; see the Metal compiler workaround.
libSystem.tbd reports unknown arm64e.x1 architecture Install an older compatible macOS SDK and leave SDKROOT unset so Pixi activation can choose it. An explicit SDKROOT is respected; see the SDK workaround.
A focused test needs a custom invocation pixi run tests --no-precompile test/<filename>.mojo omits package precompilation; keep include/linker settings consistent with the wrapper.

The canonical coding standards and test wrapper remain at their repository paths. Build documentation when examples or contracts change.

item.title: Test and hardware coverage
item.description:
These checks establish different facts. A rejected program checks a compiler contract; a host test checks host execution; successful device compilation does not establish actual accelerator execution.

Compile-contract commands

Run these commands from the repository root in the test environment. Positive controls must compile, negative controls must fail for the expected diagnostic, and intentional exclusions must remain accepted.

Contract Command
Type-only struct invariants and exclusions pixi run -e test python test/check_struct_constraints.py
Iterator mutability, filters, and borrows pixi run -e test python test/check_iteration_contracts.py
Explicit backend selection and unsupported combinations pixi run -e test python test/check_execution_backend_contracts.py
Threaded eligibility, captures, resource access, and fallback pixi run -e test python test/check_threaded_contracts.py
Ordinary/adapted resource representations and capabilities pixi run -e test python test/check_resource_contracts.py
Synchronization view/guard confinement and backend restrictions pixi run -e test python test/check_synchronization_contracts.py
Read-only spatial registration filters pixi run spatial-filter-checks
Duplicate resource/type-list fixtures pixi run test-resource-compile-failures

The full pixi run tests test wrapper runs the first seven families and the thread-capacity Python tests. Focused world_entity_iterator, execution_backend, threaded_execution, resource_adapter, and synchronization test files trigger their corresponding family. The last table row is separate. The struct checker uses type-only bindings so constructor checks cannot conceal a missing declaration invariant; see the constraint audit.

Runtime evidence

Result What it establishes
Compile pass for device code The installed compiler accepts that specialization; no hardware behavior is proved.
Host correctness pass Assertions ran on the host, including actual worker overlap where a test checks it.
Device SKIP, or an early guard returning before a launch Host/setup or compile coverage only; no device execution.
A device launch completes and output assertions pass Execution on the named device for that workload and toolchain.

has_accelerator() describes compilation support. Runtime context creation can still fail. The particle programs probe both and print explicit device PASS or SKIP evidence. Some older GPU tests return early on unsupported targets while the file still reports PASS; inspect the guard and logs, rather than counting file passes as device coverage. ExecutionBackend.DEVICE itself has no host fallback.

Record compiler/build, OS, processor/device, revision, executed path, assertions, and skips separately. The Linux/macOS CI matrix does not imply NVIDIA, AMD, or Apple device coverage merely from runner names. A source or driver change can invalidate earlier evidence; current status is in the compatibility reference, and durable backend investigations remain in the evidence map.

Markers and diagnostics

test/run_tests.sh enables ASAN, -g, -DASSERT=all, and Tracy linkage. # SKIP_ASAN opts a file out of sanitization; # SKIP_DEBUG omits debug info. Every test that launches a GPU kernel needs # SKIP_DEBUG because of the Metal compiler failure. Neither marker means that the test may skip its assertions. The doctest runner uses assertions and Tracy linkage, but does not enable the test wrapper’s ASAN/debug defaults.

CI bounds test compilation concurrency with --parallel 2 and retains output/memory/ diagnostics. An interrupted runner or missing artifact is not a correctness pass. See the CI workflow and the memory monitor for the recorded process boundary; keep performance measurements isolated from builds.

item.title: Change an ECS contract
item.description:
Use this workflow when a change affects ownership, storage, query membership, execution, safety, compatibility, or measured costs. It follows the existing repository guidelines and ADR workflow.

  1. Locate the current requirement and relevant decisions in the design map. Check status and supersession before treating a decision as current. Verify behavior in src/larecs and focused tests; acceptance alone does not prove implementation.
  2. For a consequential choice, add the next numbered file in docs/design/decisions/ using the index’s metadata schema and Context, Decision, Rationale, Consequences, and Evidence sections. Mark unaccepted ideas proposed. To replace an accepted choice, retain the old record, mark it superseded, and update the index and requirements.
  3. Update implementation and representative correctness/compile-contract tests together. For row movement, preserve typed lifecycles, live identities, location repair, bounded membership, and invalidation. For execution, check fallback, empty matches, cleanup, binding lifetime, and unsupported targets. Use architecture to trace affected mechanisms.
  4. Add or update representative benchmarks for changes to storage, queries, classification, movement, or execution costs. Follow the methodology and regression operation; a passing broad threshold does not prove zero overhead.
  5. Update visible application consequences in guides, exact contracts in the reference/docstrings, and changed mechanisms in architecture. Extract runnable listings from checked sources, regenerate affected figures, and run the documentation build.

Keep unfinished tasks and priorities in the roadmap, and completed release history in the changelog. Research notes and thesis alternatives remain evidence with their original status; they do not create a second requirements or documentation-policy system. The canonical coding standards also govern listings and API docstrings.

item.title: Build documentation and figures
item.description:
Run the publishing checks after changing a page, example, API contract, or figure. Work from the repository root with the locked setup. The pipeline retains Modo; mojo doc supplies declarations, Modo extracts examples and generates Markdown, and Hugo renders the site.

Prepare the generation environment

Install the root and documentation environments, then the pinned Chromium build:

pixi install --locked
pixi install --locked --manifest-path scripts/pixi.toml
pixi run --manifest-path scripts/pixi.toml playwright install chromium

Generation supports Linux x86-64 and macOS Apple Silicon. pixi.lock pins Mojo, MAX, and tracing dependencies; scripts/pixi.lock pins Python, Modo, Hugo, Typst, Playwright, and the native macOS Go toolchain. Linux CI uses Ubuntu 24.04, supported by the pinned Playwright release, and installs Chromium’s system libraries with playwright install --with-deps chromium. On Apple Silicon, the wrapper builds the installed Modo release natively and caches it under scripts/.pixi/; Linux uses its bundled executable.

Build and verify

Run the publishing command before committing a documentation change:

pixi run verify-docs

The command performs these checks:

  1. Clear generated Markdown and tests, regenerate compiler JSON, and run Modo with strict coverage and cross-reference checks.
  2. Compare the source-derived doctest inventory with every extracted file. Compile and execute all extracted tests, all particle stages, and every program referenced by an example shortcode. There is no exclusion list.
  3. Verify backend, resource/type-list, and spatial-registration rejection diagnostics with the existing compiler-contract checks. Their valid controls and the checked spatial stage must still compile.
  4. Re-export every non-helper figure to a temporary directory and reject differences from the committed SVGs.
  5. Build Hugo into an empty destination. Check every symbol/source target, root export, ordinary site link, repository evidence path, image, anchor, legacy redirect, and indexed search destination.
  6. Exercise failure fixtures and a second deployment prefix. Chromium checks search navigation, retained redirect fragments, mobile navigation, 360/768/1440-pixel layouts, expanded long declarations, and SVG canvases in both themes. Requests are served from generated files through browser interception; no server or live website is required.
  7. Delete generated outputs and regenerate compiler JSON, Markdown, tests, metadata, and HTML. Require byte-identical files at the same revision and base URL. Programs execute once; the second extraction must match the files that executed.

pixi run build-docs runs steps 1–5 for a shorter edit cycle. Use pixi run --manifest-path scripts/pixi.toml test-docs to rerun integration fixtures after a build. The published files are in docs/site/public/. Generated JSON, Markdown, tests, and HTML are disposable outputs; commit the source pages, templates, programs, figure sources, and SVG exports.

The example log and output/docs/examples.json record actual device execution separately from hardware skips. A successful compilation or host assertion is not device coverage. Set DOCS_REQUIRE_DEVICE=1 before either build command on an accelerator machine to reject skips. CI can publish host-checked docs without claiming accelerator execution. Browser screenshots and layout evidence are in output/docs/browser/; inspect labels and captions there when a figure or stylesheet changes. Automated checks cannot judge an explanation’s clarity.

Keep warnings fatal

Strict checks now apply to the complete generated tree. Missing alias/field descriptions and malformed cross-references were repaired before enabling Modo’s strict: true. Declarations are URL-encoded between Modo and Hugo so compiler-generated backticks cannot become false cross-references; the exact compiler declaration remains available. The wrapper rejects Modo errors, documentation warnings, and hook failures even when the packaged Linux launcher returns zero. Hugo also runs with --panicOnWarning; the wrapper rejects its template warnings.

All eight historical doctest exclusions are retired:

Former label or source Checked replacement or retirement
HostStorage_add_entity_comps HostStorage_add_entity asserts individual creation.
HostStorage_add_query_comps HostStorage_add_components checks filtered batch addition.
HostStorage_remove_query_comps HostStorage_remove_components checks filtered batch removal.
HostStorage_apply The commented historical example is no longer generated; current mutation uses the checked structural-change guide.
Query_query_init Removed Query API; the queries/iteration doctest checks the current locked range.
Query_query_without Removed Query API; the same checked guide covers exclusion filters.
larecs_readme The shared particle program replaces the duplicated introduction example.
Scheduler_scheduler The scheduler doctest now has a complete main and executes.

A partially missing extraction fails as well as an empty directory. New warnings must be fixed in the source or renderer; do not add a warning baseline or omit a program to make the build pass.

Add a checked excerpt

Keep a complete program with result assertions under examples/particles/. Mark one coherent excerpt with # region NAME and # endregion NAME, then include it and offer the full program:

{{< example file="particles/movement.mojo" region="kernel" >}}
{{< example file="particles/movement.mojo" full=true >}}

The runner includes all particle programs and automatically includes referenced programs elsewhere under examples/. Missing files, missing/empty/unbalanced regions, unchecked inline Mojo fences, and missing entry points fail. Keep required types, filters, kernels, and systems visible before explaining them. Short standalone inline examples may use Modo’s labelled doctest blocks; global=true requires a complete def main() raises:. Hide imports only.

Export figures and inspect the site

Edit the self-contained Typst/CeTZ sources, then update their exports:

pixi run figures
pixi run verify-docs

The figure build pins CeTZ 0.5.2, uses --ignore-system-fonts with committed Inter fonts, and exports every non-helper docs/figures/*.typ. Commit each source and docs/site/static/images/<name>.svg together. Keep its caption, alt text, and interpretation aligned. SVGs retain a light canvas in both themes and scroll within the reading column on narrow screens. The figure catalog records provenance.

Use pixi run serve-docs after a build, or pixi run watch-docs while editing. The watch loop supports iteration; verify-docs is the publishing gate. Repository PR previews use https://larecs.github.io/larecs/pr-preview/pr-<number>/ through the publishing workflow.

Keep links and incoming URLs working

Use api for symbols, built-site paths for pages, and repo for repository records outside docs/src. Repository/source/example links use the checkout’s HEAD revision; publish a committed checkout. Keep the initializer’s Exports: list aligned with imports. Inherited or compiler-synthesized members link to their owning source declaration.

Guide compatibility routes and heading IDs are checked against the incoming-URL fixture. Generated API aliases also retain method and overload fragments. On a case-sensitive host, System/ redirects independently of the system/ module. On a case-insensitive filesystem, the module landing page handles the legacy capitalized URL without overwriting its own content. Keep these checks when changing paths; a redirect must preserve both the base URL and incoming hash.

item.title: Measure an implementation change
item.description:
Use representative workloads to compare a storage, query, movement, or execution change. We validate semantic equivalence before interpreting elapsed time; application profiling starts in Measure and tune a simulation.

Benchmark methodology

Build a focused manual driver once with pixi run mojo build -I src benchmark/<benchmark_filename>.mojo -o /tmp/larecs-benchmark, then run /tmp/larecs-benchmark repeatedly. Run the complete manual suite with pixi run mojo run -I src benchmark/run_benchmarks.mojo.

When changing storage, queries, classification, row movement, or execution costs, add or update representative benchmarks using these criteria:

  • Keep the combined PR performance checks near one minute per runner, including compilation, warmup, and sampling. Measure cold compilation and execution separately on Linux and macOS before expanding the suite. Keep large worlds, GPU cases, and the complete benchmark registry in focused manual drivers.
  • Use deterministic inputs, bounded calibration or fixed iteration counts, and a compact scenario matrix. Spatial cases should cover uniform, dense, sparse, and moving entities with different maintenance cadences.
  • Compare identical entities and semantic work, with an unchanged-layout control. Measure isolated operations and complete frames when useful. Include input updates, classification, sorting, movement, location repair, and transfers whenever they belong to the claimed workload. State excluded setup and maintenance costs; validate results, locations, and payload preservation outside the timer, and consume results to prevent dead-code elimination.
  • Build each timing binary once, then run it repeatedly. Compare the same current driver against baseline and current libraries on the same runner with matching compiler versions and optimization settings. Use optimized builds without debug info, sanitizers, or tracing. Run builds and measurements sequentially, with no competing benchmark jobs, and report compilation separately.
  • Warm both binaries, alternate baseline/current order, and use repeated paired samples. Keep machine-specific timing baselines out of the repository. See PR performance checks and spatial checks for baseline selection, thresholds, confirmation, and support for revisions predating the spatial API.
  • Keep the small regression checks in pixi run tests test on Linux and macOS; focused test-file runs omit performance checks. Investigate sustained failures and document evidence before changing thresholds; use dedicated measurements for smaller regressions.
  • Keep scenario matrices and expected-case manifests synchronized. Invalid or incomplete reports, build failures, and correctness failures must fail checks. Update the regression reference when changing cases, timing boundaries, sampling, or baseline selection. Record hardware, compiler, method, and limitations with performance claims; track unmeasured benefits and remaining work in the roadmap.

Focused driver selection

Mechanism Checked driver and evidence
Exact selections and structural batches benchmark/entity_selection_benchmark.mojo; selection reports.
Implemented threaded engine benchmark/threaded_execution.mojo; threaded report.
Scalar atomics and uncontended guards benchmark/synchronization_benchmark.mojo; protocol and limits.
Dirty classification benchmark/dirty_spatial.mojo; deferred maintenance report.
Growable partition placement benchmark/partitioned_spatial.mojo; current and historical layouts.
Ordinary and adapted resources benchmark/resource_execution_benchmark.mojo and benchmark/resource_adapter_benchmark.mojo; resource report.

For a new comparison, retain hardware/OS, compiler build, both library revisions, driver hash, flags, warmup/calibration, paired raw samples, correctness results, and excluded costs. If a historical record lacks a field, label it unknown rather than reconstructing a claim from a machine name. Keep timing reports separate from application instructions and from the roadmap’s unfinished work.

item.title: Operate regression checks
item.description:
This reference describes scripts/check_performance.py and its bounded CPU suites. Run commands from the repository root after setup. The methodology governs new cases; historical gate costs are measurements, not runtime promises.

PR-to-PR performance checks

pixi run performance-check --base <revision> compares the current library with another Git revision on the same machine. Without --base, local runs compare the working tree against committed HEAD; GitHub PR runs use the exact PR base SHA, and main-branch push runs use the previous push commit. The tested current revision is the checkout SHA (normally the PR merge commit in CI). The complete pixi run tests test command runs the gate on Linux and macOS following correctness tests. Focused test-file runs omit it.

The coordinator builds the same current driver against both source trees with the installed Mojo compiler, using optimized builds without tracing, debug information, or sanitizers. It warms both binaries, then runs five pairs, alternating baseline/current order. A case becomes a candidate only if four pairs and the paired medians show over 30% slowdown and over 500 ns extra operation/frame time. Candidates are checked in a fresh five-pair round; only candidates recurring in both rounds fail. Invalid/incomplete reports, incorrect results, compilation failures, unavailable baselines, and timeouts fail rather than silently skipping coverage.

The two focused drivers avoid the expensive complete benchmark registry:

Core case Sizes Timed work Excluded setup and validation
access 512/2,048 matching rows Stable-ID component reads and integer checksum World construction; exact per-entity payload checks
query 512/2,048 matching rows Fresh filtered iterator, row visits, and checksum Construction of two matching archetypes and equally many excluded tag-only rows; payload checks
execute 512/2,048 rows Ordinary host dispatch and integer increments Construction; check every row’s accumulated increments
selected_execute 64 selected rows amid 512/2,048 background rows Host dispatch over a reusable contiguous selection Construction and selection creation/release; selected and untouched-row checks
selected_mutation Same selection/background sizes Add/remove a tag, including partial-archetype movement and location repair Construction; final membership, absence of tags, payload, and background-location checks
batch_cycle 512/2,048 rows Batch creation, payload initialization, removal, and recycling World construction and first validation/warmup cycle; recycled payload, membership, and surviving control-row checks

Core calibration doubles from 8 to at most 8,192 operations, stopping at 5 ms per case. Fast cases can reach the cap first. Each duration is per complete operation, not per entity. Read cases consume the checksum inside the timer; execution writes are checked after timing, with observable lengths consumed inside the timer. Spatial timing boundaries and the case matrix are below.

Run one driver with pixi run core-benchmarks or pixi run spatial-benchmarks. Select a gate with pixi run performance-check --suite core --base <revision> or --suite spatial; repeat --suite to select multiple drivers. The original pixi run spatial-performance-check remains a spatial-only compatibility command.

Reports default to the ignored output/performance/ directory; use --output to choose another directory. report.json includes the schema version, requested/resolved/effective baselines, current checkout SHA and dirty state, driver SHA-256 hashes, compiler, OS/CPU, thresholds, compilation and sampling costs, all paired measurements, and both confirmation rounds when needed. summary.md gives median times, paired changes, candidates, and confirmed failures. Candidates whose confirmation did not finish are labeled unconfirmed; only a completed confirmation can label a candidate transient. Process logs retain build, warmup, execution, and error diagnostics. GitHub adds the Markdown to the job summary and uploads the reports/logs as performance-<runner>-<attempt> artifacts for 30 days, including failed checks. This uses read-only PR permissions and works without publishing PR comments. Require the existing build/test checks in branch protection to enforce the gate.

There are no checked-in machine-specific golden timings. Driver changes affect both sides; compare historical evidence only when hashes and environments are compatible. Compiler upgrades do not measure compiler-to-compiler changes. These broad thresholds target substantial regressions on shared runners; smaller or cumulative regressions, larger worlds, heap-backed payloads, disjoint selections, and device costs need focused measurements or future coverage. See decision 0011 and the roadmap.

Small spatial benchmarks on every PR

Run pixi run spatial-benchmarks for one bounded CPU-only comparison, or pixi run spatial-performance-check --base <revision> for a regression check. The complete pixi run tests test command runs this suite through the shared coordinator after successful correctness tests, on both Linux and macOS PR runners. Focused test-file runs omit it. The existing 100,000-row maintenance benchmark and the full benchmark suite remain manual measurements.

The small driver uses 512 and 2,048 entities, one archetype, an integer cell key and a 128-byte SIMD payload per row. It inserts rows in a deterministic scrambled order, then compares the same stable-ID cell visits before and after spatial ordering. Its 32 cases cover:

Workload Cell distribution Timed work
Static cell aggregates Uniform: 8 entities/cell Read keys and all payload lanes; sum and square each cell’s aggregate
Static cell aggregates Dense: 64 entities/cell Same operation, with fewer occupied cells
Static cell aggregates Sparse: 8 entities/cell, key gaps of 1,024 Same operation across nonconsecutive occupied keys
Maintenance alone All three distributions Clean explicit boundary, or reverse keys via stable-ID access and sort/move/repair every pass
Moving cell aggregates Uniform Update every entity’s cell, aggregate cells, maintain every frame or every fourth frame

Static workload timing excludes construction, registration, and the initial maintenance pass. Mobile timing includes input updates and the selected maintenance cadence; its scrambled control performs the same updates and cell visits without maintenance. Maintenance-only reversal and conservative marking via mutable stable-ID access are included in timing. A clean ordered boundary uses deferred maintenance in the current library and full classification in older baseline libraries. This is an intentional maintenance-contract change; use the dedicated dirty-classification report for an explicit full-scan control. Checksums validate aggregate results and payload preservation, and a query validates maintenance’s output order, outside the timer. These are synthetic cell aggregates; full neighborhood algorithms, additional archetypes, transfer costs, and larger working sets remain separate measurements.

Each batch doubles from 8 to at most 8,192 frames, stopping once it takes 20 ms. The checker compiles the same current driver against the current library and the PR’s base commit, warms both binaries, then collects five paired runs with alternating execution order. It reports median frame times and paired changes for both ordered and scrambled controls. A case fails only when at least four pairs show both over 30% slowdown and over 500 ns extra time, and the paired medians exceed those thresholds. A suspected regression must recur in a fresh five-pair run. This broad threshold catches substantial regressions on shared runners; smaller changes need dedicated measurements. No machine-specific timing baseline is checked in.

The baseline comes from the GitHub PR event’s base SHA. Local runs default to committed HEAD; pass --base to compare another revision. An unavailable full SHA is fetched over public HTTPS. Since release PR #174 predates the spatial API, spatial PR #175 bootstraps against 42234f3b43d4dda58a674842374115f78ec2f08d, the implementation before this benchmark addition. Subsequent PRs whose base has the spatial API use their actual base. Compilation, malformed/missing records, checksum failures, and sustained regressions all fail the check.

item.title: Design and evidence map
item.description:
The canonical records stay at their repository paths. Links here resolve at the same revision as the generated API, preserving front matter, supersession, cross-links, and durable evidence. We do not infer implementation from acceptance.

Source Authority and use
Design index Complete ADR index, lifecycle meanings, metadata schema, and recording workflow.
ECS requirements Accepted contracts with evidence and explicit implementation gaps.
Repository architecture map Source-level overview; published architecture expands current mechanisms.
Development reference Canonical coding/docstring standards and detailed platform workarounds.
Glossary Shared terminology for composition, storage, execution, and ownership.
Roadmap Unfinished work and priorities.
Changelog Completed release history.

Decisions

The statuses below identify how to read the records; qualifications in their front matter remain authoritative. Current behavior is checked against source and tests in architecture.

Records Status and boundary
0001 selections, 0002 device execution, 0003 grid stride, 0004 errors Accepted; current selection/execution foundations.
0005 spatial ordering, 0010 full maintenance Superseded by 0012; retain historical classification/movement rationale.
0006 partitions, 0008 dirty identities, 0009 typed movement, 0012 deferred maintenance Accepted; current spatial foundations.
0007 special Cluster component Rejected; not a component users must add.
0011 regression checks Accepted; gate operation describes the implemented checker.
0013 bounded blocks Superseded by 0014; the historical 256-row cap is not current.
0014 growable stores Accepted; current partition layout.
0015 terminology Superseded by 0023; preserves beta spelling migration.
0016 synchronization Accepted, partially implemented; standalone primitives exist, dedicated kernel bindings and collection domains do not.
0017 deferred access Proposed; no callable deferred-access API.
0018 adapters Superseded by 0020 and extended by 0022; preserve source/view and lifetime rationale.
0019 threaded execution Superseded by 0020; its feasibility evidence is historical.
0020 plain values Accepted; threaded execution remains experimental.
0021 device-copy reuse, 0022 mutable adapters Accepted, experimental; implemented contracts are checked against transfer and adapter tests.
0023 explicit targets, 0024 storage ranges Accepted; current target selection and bounded ranges.

Research and historical evidence

Research describes the revision and question it investigated. Old on_device spellings, mutable-adapter experiments, or a recommended design are not current APIs. A probe may depend on its recorded toolchain rather than the current one.

Repository evidence Scope
Host-thread investigation Feasibility findings and prototype measurements; not the implemented engine. Companion dispatch probe and benchmark retain that experiment.
GPU synchronization survey Upstream primitive/backend evidence supporting 0016, with coverage limitations.
Apple publication ordering M4 correctness/performance evidence for release-store/acquire-load publication.
Storage range migration Cursor-sharing evidence and timing samples affected by concurrent builds; no controlled speedup claim.
Struct constraint audit Mojo 1.0 declaration invariants, proof limits, and intentional exclusions.
Reference invalidation probe Escaped-reference behavior motivating explicit device-copy invalidation.
Resource-view probe, trait-dispatch probe Resource descriptor and trait-dispatch experiments; production behavior comes from current adapters/tests.

Measurement reports preserve historical benchmark material with its environment, method, and missing metadata called out. Thesis figures supply visual vocabulary; their adaptation is recorded in the figure catalog. Thesis-specific systems, memory headers, bounded layouts, or branch experiments establish no current Larecs guarantee.

item.title: Measurement reports
item.description:
These scoped records retain benchmark investigations and their limitations. They describe the recorded hardware, toolchain, revision, and workload rather than promising application performance. Missing metadata is identified explicitly. Use the methodology for new measurements and the regression reference for current gate operation.

Report Evidence boundary
Selections and shared host setup Early incomplete sample, controlled M4 setup comparison, and range-migration evidence.
Threaded host execution Implemented engine on Ryzen 5850U; separate historical prototype link.
Synchronization protocol Driver timing boundaries; no recorded timing result.
Deferred dirty classification M4 sparse/full comparisons, marking costs, and default-path gate evidence.
Partition layouts Linux growable stores and explicitly historical macOS bounded blocks.
Resource execution M4 source/adapter and staged-publication costs.
AoS plotting workflow Dynamic publishing-run artifact; environment limits and raw-result access.
Regression-check runtime Initial local and hosted gate costs; no cross-platform speed comparison.

Additional investigations retain their original paths in the design and evidence map, including host-dispatch prototypes, Apple GPU publication, and storage-range migration.
